short: A failed uprising aimed at preventing Mary I's marriage to Philip of Spain and replacing her with Elizabeth.
full:
Motivated by intense xenophobia and fear that a Spanish alliance would subordinate England to Habsburg interests, a group of Protestant nobles planned a multi-pronged rebellion in early 1554. The uprising was designed to depose Mary I before her marriage to Philip of Spain, intending to replace her with her half-sister, Princess Elizabeth, who would then marry the English noble Edward Courtenay.

The conspiracy leaked, forcing the plotters to act prematurely. Only the Kentish contingent, led by Sir Thomas Wyatt the Younger, managed to raise a substantial force. Wyatt marched on London but found the city gates barred and his route blocked by royalist troops. The rebellion quickly collapsed. Wyatt and his co-conspirators were executed, and the uprising provided Mary with the pretext to execute Lady Jane Grey and briefly imprison Elizabeth in the Tower of London.
